newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Kabila set to take charge in new Congo.
newsitem.headline: Kabila set to take charge in new Congo.

text.p: Zaire's new head of state Laurent Kabila has arrived in Kinshasa to take charge after his guerrillas toppled veteran dictator Mobutu Sese Seko.
He is expected to unveil his new transitional government for Africa's third largest country. Western powers want this to be broad based and focused on steering the nation to elections.
Kabila, who proclaimed himself head of state of the renamed Democratic Republic of Congo, arrived after dark on Tuesday from Lubumbashi, the provisional rebel base on the Zambia border.
Thousands of residents of the capital of five million people had earlier gathered on the airport road to get their first glimpse of the 56-year-old veteran guerrilla leader.
Most had gone home by the time Kabila flew in. He was whisked away amid heavy security by his victorious soldiers to the riverside residence of Mobutu's last prime minister.
As Kabila arrived, gunmen in uniform shot dead two Frenchmen in Kinshasa, a French diplomat said.
The precise identities of the attackers and their motive were not immediately clear.
The two long-term residents of the country, Michel Tournaire and Herve Rigaud, were leaving a factory in western Limete district around 7.00 P.M (1800 GMT) when they were killed.
France was a close friend of Mobutu. Residents say there has been an undercurrent of anti-French feeling in Kinshasa in the final days of his 32-year strongman rule.

Rebel spokesmen had sounded warnings of a plot by diehard Mobutu loyalists to start killing foreigners to provoke intervention by their governments. France, Britain, the United States, Belgium and Portugal stationed troops in nearby Congo to evacuate foreign nationals from Kinshasa if necessary.

Soldiers of Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL) captured Kinshasa on Saturday, completing a stunning seven-month drive from the eastern border. Mobutu's ragged army offered little resistance along the way.
Kabila's envoys have been consulting politicians and business leaders in Kinshasa since Monday on a new government.

National radio, renamed Voice of Congo, said members of Kabila's alliance were "in consultation with political personalities, notably Etienne Tshisekedi", the most prominent member of the internal political opposition to Mobutu.

Scores of Tshisekedi supporters chanted his name by his residence. A dispute over the venue, with Tshisekedi insisting that Kabila envoys come to his house, had delayed talks, opposition sources said.
One newspaper, Le Potentiel, predicted that Kabila would make Tshisekedi his prime minister for the transition to a new constitution and, ultimately, full-scale elections.
Mobutu, who has cancer, prolonged his stay in the West African state of Togo on health grounds after his flight into exile left him "very, very weak", a government source said.
He arrived in the Togolese capital Lome on Sunday night on a Russian-made cargo plane from his jungle palace Gbadolite in the extreme north of his country.

Alliance finance adviser Mawampanga Mwana Nanga told reporters a promise to hold elections within one year would be kept, but that Mobutu's supporters would be excluded from a transitional government.
China joined the growing list of nations recognising Kinshasa's new rulers. Western powers have generally voiced cautious backing, linking this to progress on democracy.
But at the United Nations, the delegation chosen by Mobutu took its old seats in the General Assembly on Tuesday without challenge, assembly officials said.
